threads.thread: Watershed management planning for Lake Mattoon and Lake Paradise
threads.summary: Commissioner Clawson announced the first meeting of the watershed management group with its consultant at the water treatment plant, then reported back on that meeting, describing a two-year plan with data collection in year one and strategy implementation in year two. A subsequent public watershed planning meeting for both lakes was announced to review findings and set goals for long-term water supply protection.
threads.commitment: City is proceeding with a multi-year watershed management plan with a consultant and holding a public watershed planning meeting on Lake Paradise and Lake Mattoon.

threads.thread: Septic systems around Lake Paradise and Lake Mattoon
threads.summary: A resident raised concerns that older, grandfathered, or uninspected private septic systems around both lakes may be leaking effluent into the water supply. Officials said they are working with the Coles County Health Department to begin inspections around Lake Paradise, and discussed that public health departments rather than the EPA hold jurisdiction, with Coles County inspections to precede coordination with Cumberland and Shelby counties.
threads.commitment: City is working with the Coles County Health Department to begin inspecting private sewage systems around Lake Paradise, with later coordination with Cumberland and Shelby counties.
threads.status: no further mention in the 2 meetings we have reviewed since

Septic System Jurisdiction & Inter-County Coordination: Council members discussed regulatory oversight of septic systems around the lakes, clarifying that public health departments hold jurisdiction rather than the EPA. Staff noted plans to start inspections in Coles County before coordinating with Cumberland and Shelby counties.

threads.thread: Bowfishing ordinance for invasive carp on Lake Mattoon
threads.summary: Resident Roy Birch asked the city to revise its ordinances to allow bowfishing for invasive carp on Lake Mattoon in line with Illinois state law, citing carp stirring up lakebed sediment and nutrients that contribute to algal blooms and affect native fish. Officials undertook to review the city ordinance against state regulations.
threads.commitment: Review the city ordinance on bowfishing on Lake Mattoon to check alignment with state regulations.

threads.thread: Water treatment plant ozone treatment trial
threads.summary: The council considered Council Decision Request 2026-2709, a lease agreement with Water Tech Solutions, Inc. for equipment to run a six-month ozone treatment trial at the Water Treatment Plant. Officials said the pilot is required under IEPA regulations to verify performance before engineering plans for a full ozone system are finalized. The lease was approved.

threads.thread: Filter #2 actuator replacement at the water treatment plant
threads.summary: The council considered a $74,868 proposal from Hydro-Kinetics to replace five 25-year-old modulating electric actuators on Filter #2 at the water treatment plant, which staff said keeps equipment consistent across plant filters and eases maintenance. The proposal passed.
threads.commitment: Council approved $74,868 to Hydro-Kinetics for replacement of modulating electric actuators on Filter #2.

threads.thread: Little Wabash Drainage Project Phase 1 piping
threads.summary: The council reviewed plans and specifications for Phase 1 piping of the Little Wabash Drainage Project and authorized bid solicitation, which passed. Resident Diane Lathrop submitted an email raising concerns that faster runoff through the new 60-inch storm sewer would worsen downstream flooding on Lake Road properties and add chemical runoff to the water supply watershed; officials undertook to meet with her about the plans and possible design changes.
threads.commitment: Approved plans, specifications, and bid solicitation for Phase 1 piping, and agreed to meet with downstream resident Diane Lathrop to review the plans and evaluate potential change orders or design amendments.
